When frpc or frps exits unexpectedly or temporarily fails to start, retry starting it at increasing intervals, capped at 10 minutes. Manual stops end recovery.

While the screen is off and connections are active, the app requests a CPU wake lock and, when Wi-Fi is the default network, a Wi-Fi performance lock to reduce interruptions from sleep. The locks are released when the screen turns on, all connections stop, or this option is turned off.\n\nThis option applies when connections run through the app\'s foreground service and may increase battery use. Results depend on the Android version and system power-saving policies.

Authorize automation apps such as Tasker and MacroDroid to start, stop and restart frpc / frps profiles through plugins or broadcasts.
Add Plugin → FRP Mobile, choose an operation and target, then save. The saved action carries the current authorization and can be triggered by Tasker conditions or tasks.

Enable Automation access and tap Copy command below. Choose start, stop or restart, then select a single profile or Profiles marked for auto-start. Stop all profiles applies to every profile.\n\nThe command preview updates with your choices and includes the current token. Once it appears, tap Copy command and run it with ADB on a computer connected to your device. The profile ID is filled in automatically; frpc and frps use the same command format.

operation selects the action:
• start: start profiles.
• stop: stop profiles.
• restart: restart profiles.
• stopAll: stop all profiles.

Start, stop and restart require one target option:
• profile_id: a single profile ID, regardless of its auto-start setting.
• target=autoStart: all profiles marked for auto-start when the command runs. This selection is independent of the global boot-start switch.

profile_id is the profile ID, rather than its display name or filename. These operations change the running state; auto-start settings are managed on the Profiles tab. stopAll applies to every profile; remove profile_id and target when using it.

Replace the operation and target arguments with one of the fragments below. Keep -n, -a and token from the copied command. Replace PROFILE_ID with the actual ID from that command.

Stop one profile:
--es operation stop --es profile_id PROFILE_ID

Start profiles marked for auto-start:
--es operation start --es target autoStart

Stop all profiles:
--es operation stopAll
Send an Intent from another app

In MacroDroid or a similar app, choose to send a broadcast and enter:

Action: %1$s
Package: %2$s
Receiver class: %3$s

Add token, operation and your chosen profile_id or target as string extras. Find the token and profile ID in the copied command.

An app holding the token can control every profile. Selecting a target only sets the scope of that command. Keep copied commands and exported Tasker tasks private.

The token is stored encrypted on this device and stays the same across app or phone restarts and app updates. Turning access off immediately revokes the token. Enabling access again generates a new token, resetting the authorization. Then copy fresh commands or re-save Tasker actions.

After a request is accepted, check the actual connection state on the Dashboard. A batch may partially complete before an error or timeout; check its targets before retrying. If Android blocks a background start, open FRP Mobile and try again.
